real: A 250-foot wall of molasses barrels bursts and chokes a Boston neighborhood
source: 1919 — the Great Molasses Flood in Boston: a giant storage tank ruptured, sending a 25- to 250-foot wave of molasses through the North End at up to 35 mph, killing 21 people.
fakes: Boston fire crews race to save a warehouse full of syrup
City declares emergency after record spill in the harbor district
Residents report eerie sweet smell for days after storm

real: A mystery blast levels 800 square miles of Siberian forest — no impact crater, no asteroid, no explanation
source: 1908 — the Tunguska event flattened an estimated 80 million trees across ~2,150 sq km of Siberia in a single airburst. No crater was found, and the cause was debated for a century.
fakes: Scientists discover new type of meteorite in remote region
Forestry service investigates sudden tree death in northern taiga
Local reports describe strange lights and loud bang at dawn

real: Two ships collide at 6:30 AM and level half a city in 23 seconds
source: 1917 — the Halifax Explosion: a munitions-laden ship and a supply vessel collided in Halifax harbor, producing the most powerful accidental explosion before nuclear weapons, killing roughly 1,600–2,000 people and destroying much of the city.
fakes: Harbor workers warn of dangerous cargo pile-up near docks
City braces for worst storm in a generation as ships take shelter
Officials debate new safety rules for commercial shipping

real: A colliery tips into a village and buries a school mid-morning
source: 1966 — the Aberfan disaster: a coal waste tip above the Welsh village of Aberfan slid into the community, killing 116 people, 111 of them children at the local school.
fakes: Miners union votes to halt operations over safety concerns
Heavy rain triggers landslides across the Welsh valleys
Government orders review of waste-tip regulations

real: A pesticide plant leaks in the night and kills thousands in a sleeping city
source: 1984 — the Bhopal gas tragedy: a methyl isocyanate leak from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, killed thousands immediately and triggered decades of long-term illness.
fakes: Factory workers report unusual smell and alarm before shift
City hospital overwhelmed as residents seek treatment
Corporate headquarters issues statement on facility safety

real: A legendary freighter vanishes on Lake Superior with its entire crew in a single storm
source: 1975 — the SS Edmund Fitzgerald, a Great Lakes freighter, sank in a storm on Lake Superior, killing all 29 crew members. It became the subject of Gordon Lightfoot's famous song.
fakes: Ship's family members launch search for the missing vessel
Lakeshore towns mourn after storm claims lives
Maritime authority investigates cause of the sinking

real: A cruise ferry capsizes in the night and sinks in just 20 minutes
source: 1994 — the MS Estonia, a passenger ferry, capsized and sank in the Baltic Sea in under 20 minutes, killing 852 people — one of the worst maritime disasters in European history.
fakes: Passengers report rough seas before ferry departs for Sweden
Rescue crews mount massive operation in freezing waters
Line faces scrutiny over vessel maintenance records

real: A dormant volcano erupts without warning and flattens a town in minutes
source: 1980 — the eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington state destroyed 600 square miles of forest, killed 57 people, and became the costliest volcanic eruption in U.S. history.
fakes: Geologists warn of increased seismic activity in the region
Authorities evacuate thousands from surrounding valleys
Airlines reroute flights around ash cloud

real: An island volcano erupts so hard the shockwave circles the globe four times
source: 1883 — the eruption of Krakatoa in Indonesia was among the most powerful in recorded history; its shockwave was heard 3,000 miles away and the tsunami it triggered killed over 36,000 people.
fakes: Merchants in distant ports report strange sounds overnight
Naval vessels report unusual waves across the ocean
Scientists debate source of the massive disturbance

real: A lake exhales a cloud of carbon dioxide and kills 1,700 people in a single night
source: 1986 — the Lake Nyos disaster in Cameroon: a sudden release of carbon dioxide from the lake suffocated an estimated 1,700 people and thousands of animals in the surrounding villages.
fakes: Villagers report strange gas smell and falling livestock
Researchers study unusual chemistry of the highland lake
Government dispatches teams after mass casualties reported

real: A hotel skywalk collapses in front of a crowd of dancers
source: 1981 — the Hyatt Regency walkway collapse in Kansas City: two suspended skywalks failed during a party, killing 114 people in what became a landmark case in structural engineering.
fakes: Hotel hosts busy social event on its upper floors
Engineers later review building's design documents
Family of a victim files lawsuit against the developers

real: A garment factory collapses in the middle of a work shift, killing 1,100
source: 2013 — the Rana Plaza collapse in Bangladesh: an eight-story garment factory building pancaked, killing 1,134 people and becoming the deadliest textile-industry disaster in history.
fakes: Workers report hairline cracks in the building overnight
Factory owners refuse to allow evacuation before shift ends
International brands distance themselves from the supplier

real: An earthquake hits at 5:12 AM and turns a city into a wall of fire
source: 1906 — the San Francisco earthquake struck at 5:12 AM, and the resulting fires burned for three days, destroying roughly 500 city blocks and killing hundreds to thousands.
fakes: Firefighters struggle as water mains rupture across the city
Survivors flee to the waterfront to escape the flames
Red Cross sets up aid camps for the displaced
